name: Papua New Guinea
official: Independent State of Papua New Guinea

story: Between 1988 and 1998, the island of Bougainville fought a war against Papua New Guinea that began over a giant copper mine, Panguna, whose profits flowed elsewhere while its waste poisoned local rivers. About 20,000 people died, in a population of perhaps 200,000. The peace deal promised a referendum, and in 2019 Bougainvilleans voted 97.7 percent for independence (bne IntelliNews). The catch is that the vote was non-binding: PNG's national parliament has the final say. 2026 is when that collision came close.

In July, Bougainville's own parliament passed the Kuri Resolution reaffirming independence, with 1 September 2027 as the target date. In August, President Ishmael Toroama told Prime Minister James Marape at a joint meeting that the result could not be "diluted by parliamentary manoeuvres." The two sides did agree that Bougainville would keep 100 percent of revenue raised on the island, from fisheries to mining, by the end of 2026, a step toward the self-sufficiency Marape insists must come first. Marape has worried aloud that independence could set a "dangerous precedent" in a country of more than 800 languages, while vowing PNG's army will never again set foot on Bougainville (1News). Around this sits big-power competition: PNG signed the Pukpuk mutual defence treaty with Australia in October 2025, and an Australian-funded PNG rugby league team helped edge out a Chinese security deal (East Asia Forum). A new country could be born in the Pacific next year, or a new crisis.
briefing.power: A parliamentary democracy and Commonwealth realm. The prime minister is elected by the 118-seat National Parliament, chosen by limited preferential voting, and coalitions shift frequently. Bougainville is an autonomous region with its own president and parliament.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister James Marape (Pangu Pati), in office since 2019.
